proposals.subtype: Compose the public REST client with credential/certificate overloads and pipeline replacements
proposals.explanation: ConfidentialLedger dispatches token-credential, certificate-only and certificate-plus-token overloads, passes a truthy certificate as tlsOptions.ca and calls core getClient with or without a credential. It supports endpoint override, prefixes package user-agent text and selects a logger. It removes ApiVersionPolicy and installs a callback adding api-version when URLSearchParams.get returns falsy, defaulting the value to 2026-02-23. It replaces redirectPolicy and installs the merge-patch policy. Constructor-local configuration is grouped on this actual function; the separately declared policies implement their own algorithms.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete customized-named file is wired as the package default by supplied index.ts, while generated-style client types/options are imported separately. Package metadata names both client and Customized files and swagger context describes hidden/generated clients. This is stronger ownership context than src placement alone, though the generated factory body is absent.

proposals.subtype: Implement trusted-host redirect handling with method rules and cached write origins
proposals.explanation: createRedirectPolicy bounds following to 20 loop iterations for 300/301/302/303/307/308. 300/301/302 require current GET/HEAD; 303 changes the method to GET, removes the body and Content-Length. isTrustedTarget checks the configured ledger scheme, effective port and equal/dot-delimited-subdomain host after case/trailing-dot normalization, before conversion. An untrusted target restores original URL/method and a defined original body, clears the cache and throws. Write requests can reuse a cached origin; write-preserving 307/308 hops stage an origin, committed after a nonredirect response below 500, with 5xx/exception cache clearing as coded. The policy reuses the request and contains no Authorization stripping, but actual downstream header handling/body replay is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The full service-specific policy and trust helper are declared in the custom implementation file, and the supplied public factory explicitly replaces the default redirect policy with this one.

proposals.subtype: Override PATCH content type for user endpoint path suffixes
proposals.explanation: createMergePatchContentTypePolicy checks exact method PATCH, parses the URL and sets Content-Type to application/merge-patch+json when the pathname matches the /app/(users|ledgerUsers)/single-segment optional-trailing-slash suffix. It overrides the header but does not transform or validate the body. The public factory installs this policy.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A concrete policy factory in the custom default-client implementation is explicitly added to the public client's pipeline.

proposals.subtype: Fetch and adapt a ledger identity certificate from a separate endpoint
proposals.explanation: getLedgerIdentity creates a core REST client for a configurable identity endpoint, logs ledgerId and GETs /ledgerIdentity/{ledgerId}. It maps ledgerTlsCertificate to ledgerIdentityCertificate alongside ledgerId, throws when either mapped value is falsy and returns the object. Its predicate checks truthiness, not string types or certificate validity; there is no local response-status branch.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete standalone helper is explicitly exported by the supplied custom public index alongside the customized default client, and its special identity-service adaptation is not part of the generic REST paging template. No generated counterpart is captured, so this remains a candidate ownership judgment.

decisions.reason: The exported default factory implements the listed overload dispatch, conditional TLS CA, core-client construction, default/version policy, and pipeline wiring at the cited lines; index.ts exports that factory. The custom-named module and separate imported client types support handwritten ownership, although the generated counterpart is not supplied. The pattern describes a reusable factory shape and generator support for client configuration is plausible. This accepts the factory as one instance on the actual ConfidentialLedger symbol, without separately counting the two policy implementations.

The policy and trust helper are wired as described, but an 'authorization-preserving' pattern would claim an effect that cannot be established without downstream pipeline behavior. Name the observed reusable shape, trusted-target redirect handling with a cached write origin, instead. Whether this redirect logic is generator-addressable remains unclear.

finding.subtype: Replace the redirect policy with trusted-target handling and cached write origins
finding.explanation: createRedirectPolicy follows selected redirect statuses for at most 20 iterations, restricts 300/301/302 to GET or HEAD, and converts 303 to GET without a body or Content-Length. isTrustedTarget requires the configured ledger scheme and effective port, and an equal or dot-delimited subdomain hostname after case/trailing-dot normalization. Untrusted targets throw and reset the URL, method and any defined original body. The policy rewrites subsequent writes to a cached primary origin, stages the target origin of write-preserving 307/308 redirects, commits it after a nonredirect response below 500, and clears it for write 5xx responses or errors. No Authorization header removal appears here, but whether credentials and bodies survive downstream resends is not shown.
finding.handwrittenRationale: createRedirectPolicy and isTrustedTarget are defined in the customized public-client module; ConfidentialLedger explicitly removes the default redirectPolicy and installs createRedirectPolicy.

decisions.reason: The custom policy checks the exact PATCH method and matching URL pathname, sets the merge-patch Content-Type header, and is installed by the public factory at the cited lines. It does not modify the body. The reusable request-content-type-override pattern and plausible generator support are supported.

The exported standalone helper does fetch and remap identity-service data, but it is not established that the SDK generator or TypeSpec can produce this cross-endpoint certificate-discovery helper from the available package/spec context. Keep the finding, but mark generatorAddressable unclear rather than yes.

finding.explanation: getLedgerIdentity creates a core REST client for a configurable identity endpoint, logs ledgerId, and GETs /ledgerIdentity/{ledgerId}. It maps ledgerTlsCertificate to ledgerIdentityCertificate alongside ledgerId, throws when either mapped value is falsy, and returns the object. Its predicate tests truthiness rather than field types or certificate validity; the helper has no explicit response-status branch.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The standalone helper is explicitly exported by index.ts with the customized public client, and its identity-service request and response adaptation are implemented in getLedgerIdentity.ts. No generated counterpart is supplied, so ownership remains a source-based judgment rather than a generated-file comparison.
